thread:
sam: kicked off envelope rotation sweep for customer payloads — starting now. hitting bursts of 429s against AWS KMS, need quick advice on throttling and progress instrumentation

alex: how big is the sweep (total objects / expected rate)?

sam: ~6M objects, scanning from S3 index. initial run: 200 workers, each doing ~30 objs/s scan; aiming for ~1000 KMS ops/s but saw spikes that triggered KMS throttles per-key

jin: don't blast the per-key limit. token-bucket per-key + global concurrency limiter works. also write per-shard checkpoints to DynamoDB so workers can resume safely

maria: +1. add a DLQ table for failed rewraps with error type and last_attempt_ts. incremental scanning + checkpoints = safe resume, avoid reprocessing everything

kms-bot: AWS KMS note: default requests/second per CMK (symmetric) ~100. quota increases possible via support. GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault have different limits — see provider docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/limits.html

sam: question: is re-wrapping idempotent? if a worker double-runs a record, is that safe?

jin: design for idempotency: store rewrap_request_id or last_rewrap_ts on the envelope metadata. if dest_key_id unchanged and rewrap_request_id matches, treat as no-op. otherwise perform rotated envelope and update metadata atomically (DynamoDB conditional update)

alex: operationally on 429s we should back off and reduce per-worker concurrency. use exp backoff + jitter and slow-start probing to detect allowed throughput

maria: CLI example to resume with checkpoints / DLQ: ```
redwood-rewrap --scan-prefix s3://cust-bucket/custX/ --workers 200 --concurrency 5 --checkpoint-table envelopes-cp --dlq-table envelopes-dlq
```

jin: also emit metrics: kms_calls_total, kms_429_count, rewrap_success_total, rewrap_failure_total, checkpoint_lag_seconds. break down by cmk_id and region. dashboards should alert on sustained 429s and rising DLQ size

sam: audit logging: we want to keep CloudTrail/Cloud Audit Logs useful without drowning consumers. recommended: run the job with a single service principal and tag all KMS requests with job_id/correlation_id, then filter by that in queries

alex: yep — use dedicated IAM role with narrow key policy, add structured log fields (job_id, shard, correlation_id). then parition logs for quick query (Athena/BigQuery).

ops-bot: deploy: rewrap-job v2 started by sam at 2026-07-16T09:12:00Z; worker-group rg-rewrap-v2

maria: on partial failures, classify errors: 429/500 -> retryable; 400/bad-ciphertext -> fatal -> DLQ. include original ciphertext blob reference, error code, and stack in DLQ record to ease debugging

sam: plan based on feedback: implement per-key token bucket + global throttler, checkpoints in DynamoDB, DLQ for fatals, metrics + alert when 429 > 50/min, run with gradual ramp (start at 25% capacity -> 50% -> full)

alex: :thumbsup: can you put a short RFC/runbook change? I'll review the risk/rollback section

sam: will draft RFC and upload runbook snippets (checkpoint schema, DLQ columns, prom/rules, and sample resume command). thanks all

maria: one more: ensure key rotation IAM/RBAC: worker role must have kms:ReEncrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey only on allowed CMKs. no broad kms:* perms. also ensure CloudTrail insight events enabled for high-volume key usage

jin: and add per-job tag to KMS requests so CloudTrail entries can be correlated to job_id for audits.

sam: perfect — i'll follow up with RFC link and start implementing the checkpoint + throttler changes.
